usageNotes: Fetches a pre-rendered RRD graph (returned as a PNG filename reference) for a specific QEMU VM on a given node; requires the VM to exist on that node and the caller to hold VM.Audit on /vms/{vmid}. The 'ds' parameter accepts a comma-separated list of RRD datasource names (e.g. 'cpu,mem,netin,netout,diskread,diskwrite'); omitting 'cf' defaults to AVERAGE. Use rrddata (get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_rrddata) instead if you need raw numeric time-series values rather than a PNG graph.

examples.summary: Get a day-view CPU and memory RRD graph for VM 101 on pve1

tips: Valid datasource names for QEMU VMs include: cpu, mem, netin, netout, diskread, diskwrite, maxcpu, maxmem.
The response contains a 'filename' string pointing to the generated PNG on the Proxmox host — the file is ephemeral and served via the web UI's file endpoint.
Use 'MAX' as the consolidation function (cf) to surface burst peaks over longer timeframes like week or month.
For programmatic time-series data (JSON array of values), use the sibling rrddata endpoint instead.
